I'm planning Story 3.1 ("Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell") for a Flutter app called Cerne (Clean Architecture: data/domain/presentation layers per feature, `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart` Either, `freezed` Failure hierarchy, `hive_ce` for local storage, DI likely via `get_it`/`injectable`). The story needs to:
1. Introduce a new `lib/features/entries/` module: `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository` port with a `create` method only, and a Hive box for entries.
2. Introduce (or extend) `lib/features/capture/` owning an "Insertion Modal" bottom sheet UI with three tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto) — this story only implements the Texto tab fully; Áudio/Foto are placeholder tabs (idle/empty, reset on open).
3. Wire the modal to a "+" entry point that should already exist as a placeholder from a previous story (Story 1.6: "Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders").
4. On Salvar, call `POST /entries` (function name `entries-create` per the project's `x-cerne-function` convention — base URL from `.env`'s `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`) with `source=manual`, close the modal.
5. Offline: the "+" entry point must be disabled with the same offline-banner treatment used elsewhere (e.g. chat send) — find if that pattern already exists anywhere in the codebase.
6. Map backend error codes to the existing sealed `Failure` hierarchy.

I need a DISTILLED report (not full file dumps) covering, with exact file paths and line numbers where relevant:
- Where is the "+" entry point placeholder from Story 1.6? What file, what widget/route, what's currently there (e.g. is it a no-op button, a TODO, a named route)?
- What does an existing feature module (e.g. `features/account`, `features/vault`, or whichever exists from epics 1-2) look like structurally — list its data/domain/presentation file tree as a pattern to mirror, and name one concrete repository implementation file as a model for `EntriesRepository`.
- Where is the sealed `Failure` hierarchy defined (`core/failure/`)? What does it look like (variant names), and is there an existing error-code-to-Failure mapper I should follow as a pattern?
- Where/how is the HTTP client configured (base URL from `.env`, `apikey` header, `Authorization: Bearer` header injection)? Is there a shared API client class already, and does it already handle the `x-cerne-function` URL construction convention?
- Where is `hive_ce` initialized/registered (box registration, adapters, DI wiring)? Show one existing box registration as a pattern.
- Where is DI configured (get_it/injectable or otherwise) — show how an existing feature registers its repository/datasource/bloc.
- Is there any existing "offline banner" or connectivity-check widget/service already built (used for chat send per the product spec) — if yes, where; if no, say clearly it doesn't exist yet.
- What does `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` currently expose that's relevant to a bottom-sheet modal, tab bar, and a "sheetUp" 0.2s entrance animation — are these tokens already present or need to be added?
- Any existing use-case/interactor pattern (e.g. in account or vault features) for calling a repository from a bloc/cubit, to mirror for "SaveTextEntry" or similar.
- Any existing `freezed`/`json_serializable` DTO pattern for request/response bodies posted to the backend, to mirror for the entries-create request/response.

Keep the report tight — this is going into a spec's "Code Map" section (annotated paths + line anchors + reuse pointers), not a narrative. Report back under 600 words, with exact `path:line` references everywhere possible.

# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow).     19	/// Every route this app shell resolves — Story 1.6's original set
    20	/// (`/boot`, `/auth`, `/reauth`, `/`, `/meus-registros`, `/planos-de-acao`,
    21	/// `/configuracoes`) plus Epic 2/spec-2-1's `/vault` lock screen. Named
    22	/// constants so no call site retypes a path literal that could drift from
    23	/// the one `GoRouter` below.
    24	abstract final class AppRoutePaths {
    25	  static const boot = '/boot';
    26	  static const auth = '/auth';
    27	  static const reauth = '/reauth';
    28	  static const vaultLock = '/vault';
    29	  static const home = '/';
    30	  static const meusRegistros = '/meus-registros';
    31	  static const planosDeAcao = '/planos-de-acao';

    35	/// The epic's ONE `GoRouter`/`redirect` (Boundaries: "never a second
    36	/// competing `redirect`") — composes [VaultRepository.currentStatus] first,
    37	/// then [SessionRepository.currentStatus] (AD-14). All three repositories
    38	/// are taken as parameters (rather than this file reaching into `sl`
    39	/// itself) purely so a test can pass fakes/mocks directly, without
    40	/// touching the global DI container; `AccountSettingsRepository` (Story
    41	/// 2.4) plays no part in `_redirect` and needs no `refreshListenable` entry
    42	/// of its own — `currentBiometricEnabled` is read synchronously at
    43	/// `/vault`'s own build time below, same convention `_redirect` already
    44	/// uses for `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`, so every fresh navigation into
    45	/// `/vault` (triggered by those two streams, as already happens today)
    46	/// already picks up the latest value correctly. (Review finding: a
    47	/// `biometricEnabledStream` entry was tried here to also cover a value
    48	/// changing while already resident at `/vault`, but go_router 18.1.1's
    49	/// `GoRouterDelegate.setNewRoutePath` short-circuits whenever the matched
    50	/// `RouteMatchList` is unchanged — which it always is here, since
    51	/// `_redirect` stays at `/vault` before and after — so the route's
    52	/// `builder` is never actually re-invoked that way; removed as dead code
    53	/// rather than kept as a misleading no-op. That's a one-time, benign gap —
    54	/// at most one extra biometric prompt on a slow-network cold boot, never a
    55	/// security or dead-end issue, since PIN fallback is untouched and there's
    56	/// no way to interrupt an in-flight native biometric dialog regardless —
    57	/// which the frozen spec's I/O matrix never promised to cover.
    58	/// `VaultLockScreen.didUpdateWidget` still defensively honors a changed
    59	/// `attemptBiometricFirst` if the widget is ever rebuilt by some other

    61	/// directly from `AccountSettingsCubit`'s independent subscription to
    62	/// `biometricEnabledStream` — unrelated to routing.

    64	/// [navigatorKey] is accepted explicitly (rather than letting `GoRouter`
    65	/// generate its own internally) so the caller — `main.dart`'s
    66	/// `ExpiryOverlayHost` — can reach the Navigator's own `BuildContext`
    67	/// through the same, public, documented key instead of reaching into
    68	/// `GoRouter`'s internal `routerDelegate` (not part of its public API).
    69	GoRouter buildAppRouter({
    70	  required VaultRepository vaultRepository,
    71	  required SessionRepository sessionRepository,
    72	  required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository,
    73	  required GlobalKey<NavigatorState> navigatorKey,

    76	    navigatorKey: navigatorKey,

   134	/// I/O & Edge-Case Matrix:
   135	/// - status not yet known (`null`) -> `/boot`, unless already there.
   136	/// - `unauthenticated` -> `/auth`, unless already there.
   137	/// - `authenticated`/`expired` -> leaves `/boot`/`/auth` for `/`; every
   138	///   other location is left alone *except* `/reauth` while already
   139	///   `authenticated` (bounced home below — `/reauth` is meant to be
   140	///   reached only by the expiry overlay's own explicit navigation while
   141	///   `expired`, code review Story 1.6) — a mid-session expiry never
   142	///   navigates away (Story 1.5 behavior preserved), and the three
   143	///   non-Home destinations stay reachable while `expired`.
   144	///
   145	/// AD-14: Epic 2's `VaultStatus` gate (RF03) is composed first, strictly
   146	/// ahead of every `SessionStatus` check below — the vault gate overrides
   147	/// any location whenever it isn't `unlocked`, and only once it is does the
   148	/// rest of this function (unchanged from Story 1.6) ever run.
   149	String? _redirect(
   150	  VaultRepository vaultRepository,
   151	  SessionRepository sessionRepository,
   152	  GoRouterState state,
   153	) {
   154	  final location = state.matchedLocation;
   155	
   156	  // AD-14 — checked before SessionStatus, per Boundaries ("`_redirect`
   157	  // checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`"). `VaultStatus.locked` is
   158	  // the default from construction (never `null`), so this never waits on
   159	  // an async warm-up the way the `status == null` boot check below does.
   160	  if (vaultRepository.currentStatus != VaultStatus.unlocked) {
   161	    return location == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock
   162	        ? null
   163	        : AppRoutePaths.vaultLock;
   164	  }
   165	
   166	  final status = sessionRepository.currentStatus;
   167	
   168	  if (status == null) {
   169	    return location == AppRoutePaths.boot ? null : AppRoutePaths.boot;
   170	  }
   171	
   172	  if (status == SessionStatus.unauthenticated) {
   173	    return location == AppRoutePaths.auth ? null : AppRoutePaths.auth;
   174	  }
   175	
   176	  // status is authenticated or expired.
   177	  // `vaultLock` is included here too: once the vault unlocks while this
   178	  // location is still `/vault` (the normal cold-start path once
   179	  // `authenticate()` succeeds), the same fall-through that already bounces
   180	  // `/boot`/`/auth` to Home applies — `/vault` is never a valid resting
   181	  // place once `VaultStatus.unlocked`.
   182	  if (location == AppRoutePaths.boot ||
   183	      location == AppRoutePaths.auth ||
   184	      location == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock) {
   185	    return AppRoutePaths.home;
   186	  }
   187	  // `/reauth` is a throwaway placeholder standing in for Epic 2's real
   188	  // reauth flow; it should never be sitting open once the session is back
   189	  // to fully `authenticated` (code review, Story 1.6).
   190	  if (location == AppRoutePaths.reauth &&
   191	      status == SessionStatus.authenticated) {
   192	    return AppRoutePaths.home;
   193	  }
   194	  return null;
   195	}

   197	/// Wraps [streams] as a single `Listenable` so `GoRouter`'s
   198	/// `refreshListenable` can re-run [_redirect] on every emission from either
   199	/// one — go_router 18.1.1 exports no `GoRouterRefreshStream` of its own
   200	/// (Code Map), so this is that small local class. Extended by AD-14 to
   201	/// subscribe to both the vault and the session streams (previously just
   202	/// the one session stream), composing them into the one `Listenable`
   203	/// `GoRouter` itself requires (Boundaries: "never a second
   204	/// `GoRouter`/`redirect`").
   205	class _GoRouterRefreshStream extends ChangeNotifier {
   206	  _GoRouterRefreshStream(Iterable<Stream<dynamic>> streams) {
   207	    _subscriptions = [
   208	      for (final stream in streams)
   209	        stream.listen(
   210	          (_) => notifyListeners(),
   211	          // Mirrors `ExpiryOverlayHost`'s and `SessionRepositoryImpl`'s own
   212	          // subscriptions to this same stream — no current implementation
   213	          // ever errors on it, but a future one that did must not surface
   214	          // as an unhandled zone exception here specifically.
   215	          onError: (_, _) {},
   216	        ),
   217	    ];
   218	  }
   219	
   220	  late final List<StreamSubscription<dynamic>> _subscriptions;
   221	
   222	  @override
   223	  void dispose() {
   224	    for (final subscription in _subscriptions) {
   225	      subscription.cancel();
   226	    }
   227	    super.dispose();
   228	  }
   229	}

7:Users capture a journal Entry through one shared Insertion Modal in three ways — typed text, recorded audio, or a photo — and every modality ends up as the same persisted `Entry` shape. Audio is transcribed entirely on-device; a photo's text is recognized server-side via OCR before the Entry exists. Text and audio/photo stay merged into one epic because an un-transcribed audio Entry or un-OCR'd photo Entry is not a usable product outcome on its own — "capture" and "process" are one milestone here, not two. The epic also guarantees interrupting any capture (switching tabs, backing out, stopping early) never leaves a stray partial or empty Entry behind. This is the first epic to introduce `features/entries/`, which every later epic that creates or reads an Entry (Timeline, Search, Chat save-to-journal) will consume through its port — so decisions made here about that port's shape are load-bearing for the rest of the app.
11:- Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell
12:- Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription
13:- Story 3.3: Photo Entry Capture & Backend OCR
14:- Story 3.4: Cancel-Safe Capture Across All Tabs
18:- All three capture modalities (text, audio, photo) must produce the same persisted Entry shape; `source` is `manual`/`audio`/`photo` respectively, and each `POST /entries` call must carry the correct one.
21:- Photo OCR calls the backend before the Entry is created, mirroring the same four-state shape: capture → processing OCR → recognized → error. `OCR_NO_TEXT` is a distinct, non-retryable outcome with two recovery paths: "Tentar novamente" (retry OCR on the same photo) and "Salvar só a foto" (save with no extracted text) — never a single generic failure message. An oversized photo returns non-retryable `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413); show a size-specific message with no retry button.
22:- Cancel-safety (FR-11) is absolute: interrupting a capture before Salvar — closing the modal, switching Insertion Modal tabs, backing out mid-photo, stopping a recording early — must never fire `POST /entries`. Opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty; switching tabs mid-capture cancels the in-flight capture outright (resolved ambiguity — the prototype itself left this undefined).
23:- Offline: the "+" entry point is disabled with the same offline-banner treatment as chat send. Capture requires a live `POST /entries` round trip (PII check + embedding), so there is no local-only queued write — a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `NetworkOffline`, never queued.

30:- Backend calls for this epic: `POST /entries` → function `entries-create`; `POST /media/ocr` → function `media-ocr` (the photo itself is not persisted server-side, only the extracted text comes back). 9	/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
10	///
11	/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
12	/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
13	@freezed
14	sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
15	  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
17	  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
18	      NetworkTimeout;
19	  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
20	      NetworkOffline;
21	  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
22	  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
23	      PiiCheckFailed;

25	      EmbeddingFailed;

32	  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
33	      PayloadTooLarge;

36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is

45	  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
